subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should temp artifact provenance and runtime-critical temp-path guardrails be a core OpenClaw default, a plugin/skill/ClawHub package, or a smaller doctor-only warning surface?
rationale: The request touches core storage defaults, cleanup authority, runtime guardrail policy, and core-versus-plugin scope, which need maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
options.body: Have core cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, leaving workflow-specific audit/review staging classification to plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full core provenance registry
options.body: Build a core-owned temp artifact registry and janitor policy for all first-class OpenClaw temp artifacts, accepting broader storage and cleanup responsibility in core.

options.title: Plugin/SOP only
options.body: Keep the broad workflow cleanup model outside core and track only concrete runtime temp-path bugs separately.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
recommendation.body: Have core cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, leaving workflow-specific audit/review staging classification to plugins or ClawHub packages.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combination of prior product-scope decision evidence and related temp-boundary commits.
